en.headline: Police record more than 20,000 scam cases in first half, losses hit HK$3.5 billion
en.dek: Investment scams accounted for about one-tenth of cases and more than HK$1.6 billion in losses; officers highlighted AI-generated personas and ongoing Fun Coffee and JPEX investigations.
body: Hong Kong police said on Friday they recorded 20,613 scam cases in the first half of 2026, with total losses amounting to about HK$3.5 billion.

Around one-tenth of the cases, or 2,151, were investment scams that accounted for more than HK$1.6 billion in losses. Commercial Crime Bureau senior superintendent Kung Hing-fun said syndicates were using AI-generated investment experts and other digital tools to lure victims into virtual-asset schemes.

Police also updated figures on two major investigations. Reports linked to the Fun Coffee alleged investment scam had risen to 273, with losses exceeding HK$113 million. The long-running JPEX case had drawn more than 2,800 reports and losses surpassing HK$1.6 billion; 29 of the 81 people arrested have been charged.
Officers urged the public to adopt a ‘doubt first, verify later’ approach and warned that celebrities or key opinion leaders who promote dubious investment products may themselves face prosecution.

zh.headline: 警方上半年錄逾2萬宗騙案 涉款約35億元 投資騙案佔逾16億
zh.dek: 約一成個案屬投資騙案；警方提到騙徒使用AI生成投資專家，並更新Fun Coffee及JPEX案數字。
body: 警方周五公布，今年上半年共錄得20,613宗詐騙案，總損失約35億元。
當中約一成即2,151宗屬投資騙案，涉款逾16億元。商業罪案調查科高級警司孔慶勳表示，騙徒利用AI生成投資專家等手法，誘使市民投資虛擬資產。
警方同時更新兩宗大型案件數字。涉「Fun Coffee」懷疑投資騙案的報案增至273宗，損失逾1.13億元；JPEX案則累計接獲逾2,800名受害人報案，涉款逾16億元，81名被捕人士中已有29人被起訴。
警方呼籲市民建立「先疑後查」意識，並提醒若以不誠實手法宣傳或推廣虛擬投資產品，可觸犯相關法例。
